title: Affine relative-dualizing realization, multiplication and localization constructions
statement:
For a commutative ring $A$, let $D(A)$ be the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $\widetilde{(-)}:D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A})$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-derived-category] as the functor of the chosen affine quasi-coherent equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], followed by inclusion. For commutative rings $R,A$ with an $R$-algebra structure, put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$ and $\mu(a\otimes a')=aa'$. Use the K-flat derived scalar extension $E_\varphi$ and diagonal $\Delta=A[0]\in D(B)$ of [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data]. Define $T_1=E_{p_1}(T)$ and $H_{R,A}(T)=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(\Delta,T_1)$, using derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Define $m_\Delta:\Delta\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\Delta\to\Delta$ by localizing ordinary multiplication of the diagonal $B$-module $A$. More generally, in an abelian braided closed monoidal category $\mathcal C$ with countable coproducts and its monoidal derived localization $Q$, define the degree-zero derived multiplication of any $m:D\otimes D\to D$ by $Q(D[0])\otimes Q(D[0])\xrightarrow{\mu_Q}Q(D[0]\otimes D[0])\xrightarrow{Q(\sigma)}Q((D\otimes D)[0])\xrightarrow{Q(m[0])}Q(D[0])$, where $\sigma$ is the ordinary single-complex tensor identification. For $F\in D(B)$ and $\gamma:\Delta\to F$, define the class map $m_\gamma:\Delta\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(\Delta,F)$ as the tensor--Hom transpose of $m_\Delta;\gamma$.

For scheme maps $f:X\to S$, $j_A:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, $j_R:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ satisfying $j_A;f=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to A);j_R$, define the product-chart map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to X\times_S X$ by the inverse affine fibre-product identification followed by the map induced by $j_A,j_A,j_R$ and this equality. Neither openness nor a Noetherian hypothesis is required for this map.

For any homomorphism $\varphi:B\to C$ of commutative rings, let $\epsilon_\varphi$ denote the left-derived counit $Q_h\,;E_\varphi\Rightarrow\varphi_*\,;Q_h$, where $\varphi_*$ here means ordinary extension of scalars on homotopy complexes and $Q_h$ is homotopy localization. Define the predicate that a family of isomorphisms $\tau_{P,Q}:E_\varphi(P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q)\cong E_\varphi P\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}E_\varphi Q$ is a normalized tensor comparison to mean naturality in both derived variables and, for every pair of homotopy complexes $P,Q$, the equation $\tau_{Q_hP,Q_hQ};(\epsilon_\varphi(P)\otimes\epsilon_\varphi(Q));\mu_{Q_h,C}=E_\varphi(\mu_{Q_h,B});\epsilon_\varphi(P\otimes Q);Q_h(\delta_\varphi(P,Q))$. Here $\delta_\varphi$ is the actual ordinary extension-of-scalars total-tensor comparison and $\mu_{Q_h}$ is the lax monoidal localization map. Given such a family (without requiring its normalization for the following definitions), define $\ell_\varphi(D,F):E_\varphi R\operatorname{Hom}_B(D,F)\to R\operatorname{Hom}_C(E_\varphi D,E_\varphi F)$ as the transpose of $\tau_{D,R\operatorname{Hom}_B(D,F)}^{-1};E_\varphi(\operatorname{ev})$. For $B=A\otimes_R A$ and $\gamma:\Delta\to F$, define the localized class map as the transpose of $\tau_{\Delta,\Delta}^{-1};E_\varphi(m_\Delta);E_\varphi(\gamma)$. These constructions introduce no flatness, finiteness, nonzero or Noetherian hypotheses.
